historical_claims.anchor: The classical chain-termination method, developed by Frederick Sanger and colleagues, uses controlled termination of DNA synthesis to determine sequence.
One of the best-known editing systems comes from microbial defense.

In a 2012 paper, Martin Jinek, Krzysztof Chylinski, Ines Fonfara, Michael Hauer, Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier demonstrated that a Cas9 nuclease could be directed to cut chosen DNA sequences with engineered RNA guides.
